patient_overview.name: María Eugenia Rosas
patient_overview.description: María Eugenia Rosas is a 43-year-old single woman living in Bloomfield, NJ, in a household of eight, who works full-time and was referred for nutrition counseling after being flagged with prediabetes, obesity, and anemia on recent labs. She is precise and factual in how she describes her health - citing her HbA1c and glucose numbers from memory - but reserved about her personal life, offering little beyond the clinical facts at first. She comes across as someone who has already decided she wants to make one concrete change but is guarded about what is actually making that hard to do.

demographics.occupation: Billing coordinator at a dental office
demographics.cultural_context: María grew up in a bilingual household and still speaks mostly her first language at home with family; English is her second language for work and most medical visits. Food was never the center of elaborate home cooking in her upbringing - her mother worked long shifts too - so takeaway and quick plates from neighborhood spots became normal early on, and that pattern has stuck as her main way of eating and socializing with coworkers and cousins. She does not see this as a cultural loss, just how her family has always eaten.

medical_history: Whiplash injury to neck (2026-07 to 2026-09, resolved)
current_symptoms: Feels tired most afternoons, especially after 3pm
Gets short of breath climbing the stairs at the dental office
Notices she is thirstier than she used to be
Occasional lightheadedness she attributes to 'low iron'
clinical_findings: Pale conjunctiva consistent with her documented anemia
Central weight distribution with BMI in the obese range
Mild fatigue evident in flattened affect during longer conversation
Normal gait and no acute distress on exam

supplements_and_otc: Over-the-counter iron tablets, taken 'sometimes, when I remember'
Ginger candies she keeps at her desk for nausea

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Eats out or orders takeaway 5-6 days a week; cooks at home rarely, mostly on Sundays when the whole household eats together
food_preferences: Rotisserie chicken plates with rice from the place next to her office
Pupusas or empanadas from a stand near her apartment on weeknights when she's too tired to cook
Sweet coffee with condensed milk in the morning
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: Portion sizes at takeaway meals - she estimates but doesn't measure
Frequency of sugary coffee and soda across the day
Whether she is eating enough iron-rich foods consistently versus relying on the supplement 'sometimes'
Skipped lunches on days she is pulled into caregiving tasks
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Breakfast: coffee only, sometimes a roll. Lunch: ordered in or picked up near work, eaten at her desk. Dinner: takeaway most nights, home-cooked only on Sundays.
nutrition_profile.hydration: Mostly diet soda and coffee during the day; drinks water inconsistently, says she 'forgets' until she's very thirsty
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Walks to the bus stop and around the office; no structured exercise; says there is 'no time' most weeks
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Does not smoke; does not drink alcohol (AUDIT-C score of 0)
nutrition_profile.sleep: Sleeps around 6 hours most nights, often interrupted

psychosocial_profile.personality: Reserved and private; keeps conversation on the facts and figures of her health rather than her feelings; warms up slowly once she senses she won't be judged
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Precise and factual - cites her HbA1c of 6.2%, her glucose reading, and exact dates of diagnoses from memory; gives short answers to open questions until trust builds; dislikes vague advice
goals: Wants one specific, concrete first step she can start this week
Wants her next HbA1c to come back lower
Wants more energy to get through her full workday
concerns: Worried prediabetes will become full diabetes like it did for her aunt
Concerned about her low hemoglobin and whether it's connected to how tired she feels
Frustrated that her schedule leaves no room to cook
beliefs: Believes numbers tell the real story more than how she feels day to day
Thinks her tiredness is 'just the anemia' and not related to her weight or diet
Believes she just needs more willpower to cook more often
motivations: Her HbA1c result scared her enough to want to act
Wants to keep working full-time without her energy giving out
Doesn't want to end up on medication if she can avoid it
fears: Fear of progressing to type 2 diabetes
Fear of being seen as weak or failing if she can't change her eating
Fear that asking for help at home will not be taken seriously
barriers: No time to cook most days due to work and caregiving responsibilities at home
Transportation problems have already caused her to miss a medical appointment
Household of eight means little control over what food is around or when she can eat
Quite a bit of self-reported stress
strengths: Organized and detail-oriented - tracks her own lab numbers and dates
Already in the preparation stage, has decided she wants to change something concrete
Higher education and comfortable researching health information on her own
psychosocial_profile.support_system: Lives in a household of eight with extended family nearby; sees people socially only 1-2 times a week outside the home; family is physically close but tends to brush off her prediabetes and anemia as 'nothing serious' and continues to serve the same heavy, convenience-based meals at gatherings
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Preparation stage - she has already decided she wants to make a change and is looking for one clear, concrete first step rather than a broad overhaul

initial_information: States her HbA1c was 6.2% and her glucose was 64.6 mg/dL on her last test, with the date
Mentions she was told her BMI is just over 30
Says she eats out most days because of her schedule
Reports feeling tired in the afternoons
discoverable_information: Describes her usual takeaway orders and typical day of eating when asked directly
Mentions missing a medical appointment because of a transportation problem
Admits she doesn't always remember to take her iron tablets
Shares that her family doesn't take her diagnoses very seriously when gatherings happen
reluctant_information: Reveals, when asked gently about her evenings, that she spends several hours after work caring for an elderly relative in the household and has almost no time left for herself
Admits this caregiving is the real reason she hasn't started cooking more, not just laziness as she first implied
hidden_information: She has quietly started skipping her own lunch some days so she can finish caregiving tasks before the relative's appointments
She feels guilty and would not bring up the caregiving role unless asked specifically and non-judgmentally about her evening routine and who else lives in the home
